explanation_en: 'Estar pendiente de' means to be attentive to, waiting for, or keeping an eye on something or someone. It is widely used in both professional and personal contexts (e.g., 'estoy pendiente de tu llamada'). Avoid confusing it with 'pendiente' as a noun (slope or earring).

examples.en_text: We are waiting to receive your confirmation to reserve the meeting room.
examples.target_text: Estamos pendientes de recibir su confirmación para reservar la sala de reuniones.

examples.en_text: Juan is keeping a close eye on his grandmother since she fell last week.
examples.target_text: Juan está muy pendiente de su abuela desde que se cayó la semana pasada.

examples.en_text: The passengers on the flight to Madrid are keeping an eye on the screens to see if there are delays.
examples.target_text: Los pasajeros del vuelo a Madrid están pendientes de las pantallas para ver si hay retrasos.

examples.en_text: Please, keep an eye on the oven while I go buy some bread.
examples.target_text: Por favor, quédate pendiente del horno mientras voy a comprar un poco de pan.

examples.en_text: I've been waiting by my phone all morning because they are calling me today about the new job.
examples.target_text: Llevo toda la mañana pendiente del móvil porque hoy me llaman para el nuevo trabajo.

examples.en_text: To organize the excursion, we have to keep an eye on the weather forecast.
examples.target_text: Para organizar la excursión, tenemos que estar pendientes del pronóstico del tiempo.

explanation_en: In news and formal contexts, 'trascender' is used to indicate that information has leaked, been revealed, or made public (often when it was meant to be private or confidential). It is a sophisticated alternative to 'hacerse público' or 'filtrarse'. It is typically used in the third person, often with negative constructions like 'no ha trascendido'.

examples.en_text: In the end, it leaked to the press that the director was going to resign.
examples.target_text: Al final, trascendió a la prensa que el director iba a dimitir.

examples.en_text: Although they tried to keep the project a secret, the news ended up leaking out.
examples.target_text: Aunque intentaron mantener el proyecto en secreto, la noticia acabó por trascender.

examples.en_text: No details have leaked out about yesterday's private meeting.
examples.target_text: No ha trascendido ningún detalle sobre la reunión privada de ayer.

examples.en_text: It is a very delicate family matter and we don't want it to get out.
examples.target_text: Es un asunto familiar muy delicado y no queremos que trascienda.

examples.en_text: Shortly after the negotiation, the first agreements of the treaty became known.
examples.target_text: Poco después de la negociación, trascendieron los primeros acuerdos del tratado.

examples.en_text: If this information leaks out, it could cause a lot of problems in the office.
examples.target_text: Si esta información trasciende, podría causar muchos problemas en la oficina.

idiom: con el miedo metido en el cuerpo
explanation_en: This highly idiomatic expression literally translates to 'with fear put into the body' and means to be deeply shaken, traumatized, or terrified after a scary event. It is used in everyday spoken Spanish to describe the lingering physical and emotional sensation of fear. It is often paired with verbs like 'seguir', 'quedarse', or 'dejar'.

examples.en_text: After the near-accident on the highway, I got home with fear in my bones.
examples.target_text: Después del casi accidente en la autopista, llegué a casa con el miedo metido en el cuerpo.

examples.en_text: Since she watched that horror movie, she has been terrified and can't sleep alone.
examples.target_text: Desde que vio esa película de terror, tiene el miedo metido en el cuerpo y no puede dormir sola.

examples.en_text: The neighbors still have fear in their bones after last week's robbery.
examples.target_text: Los vecinos todavía tienen el miedo metido en el cuerpo tras el robo de la semana pasada.

examples.en_text: I walked through the dark alley with fear in my bones, thinking someone was following me.
examples.target_text: Caminé por el callejón oscuro con el miedo metido en el cuerpo, pensando que alguien me seguía.

examples.en_text: The tremor only lasted ten seconds, but it left us terrified for hours.
examples.target_text: El temblor solo duró diez segundos, pero nos dejó con el miedo metido en el cuerpo durante horas.

examples.en_text: He spoke with the director and came out of the office with fear in his bones.
examples.target_text: Habló con el director y salió de la oficina con el miedo metido en el cuerpo.

explanation_en: 'Poner en valor' is a very common journalistic and political collocation meaning to highlight, appreciate, or showcase the worth of something that might otherwise be overlooked. It is a more sophisticated and professional alternative to 'valorar' or 'destacar'. It is frequently used when discussing heritage, public services, or collective efforts.

examples.en_text: It is necessary to highlight the value of our town's historical heritage to attract more tourists.
examples.target_text: Es necesario poner en valor el patrimonio histórico de nuestro pueblo para atraer más turistas.

examples.en_text: In the job interview, you must showcase your previous experience in the sector.
examples.target_text: En la entrevista de trabajo, debes poner en valor tu experiencia previa en el sector.

examples.en_text: The new exhibition highlighted the value of the work of 20th-century women artists.
examples.target_text: La nueva exposición puso en valor el trabajo de las mujeres artistas del siglo XX.

examples.en_text: We want to showcase the local and organic products of the region.
examples.target_text: Queremos poner en valor los productos locales y ecológicos de la región.

examples.en_text: It is important that the company values the effort of its employees.
examples.target_text: Es importante que la empresa ponga en valor el esfuerzo de sus empleados.

examples.en_text: This project will serve to showcase the talent of young designers.
examples.target_text: Este proyecto servirá para poner en valor el talento de los jóvenes diseñadores.

explanation_en: 'Echarse la noche (encima)' is an idiomatic way to say that night is falling or darkness is rapidly approaching, often carrying a connotation of urgency or pressure. It is a pronominal construction ('se echa'). You can also use it figuratively when a deadline is fast approaching (e.g., 'se nos echa el tiempo encima').

examples.en_text: We decided to return to the campsite because night was already falling.
examples.target_text: Decidimos regresar al campamento porque ya se echaba la noche.

examples.en_text: I was so focused on working in the garden that I didn't realize night was falling.
examples.target_text: Estaba tan concentrado trabajando en el jardín que no me di cuenta de que se echaba la noche.

examples.en_text: We had to look for a hotel quickly because night was falling upon us on the road.
examples.target_text: Tuvimos que buscar un hotel de prisa porque se nos echaba la noche encima en la carretera.

examples.en_text: We quickened our pace when we saw that night was falling and the streets were becoming empty.
examples.target_text: Aceleramos el paso al ver que se echaba la noche y las calles se quedaban vacías.

examples.en_text: They couldn't find the way back and night was falling upon them without flashlights.
examples.target_text: No encontraban el camino de vuelta y se les echaba la noche encima sin linternas.

examples.en_text: As night was falling, we lit the fireplace and prepared dinner.
examples.target_text: Mientras se echaba la noche, encendimos la chimenea y preparamos la cena.

explanation_en: This classic idiomatic adverbial phrase means 'from a bird's-eye view' or 'from above.' It is widely used in journalism, literature, and everyday speech to describe aerial perspectives or to give a broad, general overview of a situation. It is always used with the preposition 'a'.

examples.en_text: From the top of the tower, you can see the entire city from a bird's-eye view.
examples.target_text: Desde lo alto de la torre, se puede ver toda la ciudad a vista de pájaro.

examples.en_text: Let's analyze the map from a bird's-eye view to plan the hiking route.
examples.target_text: Vamos a analizar el mapa a vista de pájaro para planificar la ruta de senderismo.

examples.en_text: The drone took some spectacular photos of the coast from a bird's-eye view.
examples.target_text: El dron tomó unas fotos espectaculares de la costa a vista de pájaro.

examples.en_text: During the helicopter ride, we enjoyed a bird's-eye view of the Grand Canyon.
examples.target_text: Durante el viaje en helicóptero, disfrutamos del Gran Cañón a vista de pájaro.

examples.en_text: The architect showed us the design of the new park from a bird's-eye view.
examples.target_text: El arquitecto nos mostró el diseño del nuevo parque a vista de pájaro.

examples.en_text: In the first class, we will do a bird's-eye overview of the course topics.
examples.target_text: En la primera clase, haremos un repaso a vista de pájaro de los temas del curso.

explanation_en: This expression is used to assert that you know something for a fact or have personal certainty about it. It is more formal and emphatic than simply saying 'sé que' (I know that). It is commonly used in legal, professional, or serious conversational contexts to assure the listener of the truth of a statement.

examples.en_text: I know for a fact that you have been studying hard for this exam.
examples.target_text: Me consta que has estado estudiando mucho para este examen.

examples.en_text: I know for a fact that she always tells the truth, so I trust her word.
examples.target_text: Me consta que ella siempre dice la verdad, así que confío en su palabra.

examples.en_text: I know for a fact that the team has made a great effort to finish the project on time.
examples.target_text: Me consta que el equipo ha hecho un gran esfuerzo para terminar el proyecto a tiempo.

examples.en_text: Don't worry, I know for a fact that he wants to resolve this misunderstanding.
examples.target_text: No te preocupes, me consta que él quiere solucionar este malentendido.

examples.en_text: We all know for a fact that this problem is not going to be solved overnight.
examples.target_text: A todos nos consta que este problema no se va a resolver de la noche a la mañana.

examples.en_text: I know for a fact that the store is closed today because it is a public holiday.
examples.target_text: Me consta que la tienda está cerrada hoy porque es un día festivo.

explanation_en: This transition phrase is used to summarize a current state of affairs, often before introducing a new development or concluding a report. It translates to 'that's how things stand' or 'as things stand.' It is very common in journalism and news broadcasts to transition between topics or wrap up a segment.

examples.en_text: We don't have enough budget for the project, that's how things are.
examples.target_text: No tenemos suficiente presupuesto para el proyecto, así están las cosas.

examples.en_text: They decided to sell our grandparents' house, and unfortunately that's how things are now.
examples.target_text: Ellos decidieron vender la casa de los abuelos, y lamentablemente así están las cosas ahora.

examples.en_text: It is difficult to find a good job without experience, that's how things stand nowadays.
examples.target_text: Es difícil encontrar un buen trabajo sin experiencia, así están las cosas hoy en día.

examples.en_text: The doctor recommended that I rest for a whole month; that's the way things are, I can't do anything.
examples.target_text: El médico me recomendó descansar un mes entero; así están las cosas, no puedo hacer nada.

examples.en_text: The government has changed the traffic laws again, that's how things are in this country.
examples.target_text: El gobierno ha cambiado las leyes de tráfico otra vez, así están las cosas en este país.

examples.en_text: They canceled our flight because of the storm and we will have to wait until tomorrow, that's how things stand.
examples.target_text: Cancelaron nuestro vuelo por la tormenta y tendremos que esperar hasta mañana, así están las cosas.

explanation_en: Using 'resultar' followed by an adjective is a very natural, native way to express how something seems to you or how you perceive it (e.g., 'me resulta difícil' instead of 'es difícil para mí'). It conveys a subjective reaction or personal experience. It is highly versatile and used across all registers, from casual conversation to formal writing.

examples.en_text: I find it very difficult to pronounce this word correctly.
examples.target_text: Me resulta muy difícil pronunciar esta palabra correctamente.

examples.en_text: Her face looks familiar to me, but I don't remember how I know her.
examples.target_text: Su cara me resulta familiar, pero no recuerdo de qué la conozco.

examples.en_text: I find it impossible to finish this report before five o'clock.
examples.target_text: Me resulta imposible terminar este informe antes de las cinco.

examples.en_text: I find it curious that he still hasn't called to confirm his attendance.
examples.target_text: Me resulta curioso que todavía no haya llamado para confirmar su asistencia.

examples.en_text: I don't find this new chair comfortable at all for working all day.
examples.target_text: Esta silla nueva no me resulta nada cómoda para trabajar todo el día.

examples.en_text: I find your explanation quite clear, now I understand the problem.
examples.target_text: Tu explicación me resulta bastante clara, ahora entiendo el problema.

explanation_en: A very common construction used to label or brand someone or something with a negative attribute (e.g., 'tachar de mentiroso' - to brand as a liar). It is always followed by the preposition 'de' and a noun or adjective. It carries a critical or judgmental tone and is frequently found in political commentary and opinion pieces.

examples.en_text: You can't label him as irresponsible just because he arrived late once.
examples.target_text: No puedes tacharlo de irresponsable solo porque llegó tarde una vez.

examples.en_text: Many branded him a liar after watching the debate.
examples.target_text: Muchos lo tacharon de mentiroso después de ver el debate.

examples.en_text: She is always afraid of being labeled as boring if she doesn't go out partying.
examples.target_text: Ella siempre tiene miedo de que la tachen de aburrida si no sale de fiesta.

examples.en_text: At first, the press branded his project as madness, but now it is a success.
examples.target_text: Al principio, la prensa tachó su proyecto de locura, pero ahora es un éxito.

examples.en_text: Don't label me as selfish for wanting to spend some time alone.
examples.target_text: No me taches de egoísta por querer pasar un tiempo a solas.

examples.en_text: It's unfair for them to brand us as lazy without knowing our work.
examples.target_text: Es injusto que nos tachen de perezosos sin conocer nuestro trabajo.

explanation_en: This pronominal verb is used to express that one action, figure, or situation results in or is equivalent to another. It is highly common in economic, political, and analytical contexts. Learners should note that it always requires the preposition 'en'.

examples.en_text: The increase in sales translates into higher profits for the company.
examples.target_text: El aumento de las ventas se traduce en mayores beneficios para la empresa.

examples.en_text: Eating a balanced diet translates into having more energy during the day.
examples.target_text: Llevar una dieta equilibrada se traduce en tener más energía durante el día.

examples.en_text: All your effort and dedication will translate into excellent grades at the end of the course.
examples.target_text: Todo tu esfuerzo y dedicación se traducirá en excelentes notas al final del curso.

examples.en_text: The new transport measures have translated into a reduction in pollution.
examples.target_text: Las nuevas medidas de transporte se han traducido en una reducción de la contaminación.

examples.en_text: The lack of organization at work translates into a waste of time and money.
examples.target_text: La falta de organización en el trabajo se traduce en una pérdida de tiempo y dinero.

examples.en_text: His anger translated into a long silence that lasted all afternoon.
examples.target_text: Su enfado se tradujo en un largo silencio que duró toda la tarde.

explanation_en: A very common transitional phrase used in both spoken and written Spanish to refer to a point further along in time or space. It is a more natural, native-sounding alternative to simply saying 'después' or 'luego'. It is frequently used in presentations, lectures, and articles to signpost upcoming information.

examples.en_text: We can talk about the project details later on.
examples.target_text: Podemos hablar de los detalles del proyecto más adelante.

examples.en_text: There is a gas station further ahead, right after the bridge.
examples.target_text: Hay una gasolinera más adelante, justo después del puente.

examples.en_text: I would like to buy a house later on, when I have a stable job.
examples.target_text: Me gustaría comprar una casa más adelante, cuando tenga un trabajo estable.

examples.en_text: If you walk a little further ahead, you will see the museum entrance.
examples.target_text: Si caminas un poco más adelante, verás la entrada del museo.

examples.en_text: We are very busy right now, so we will make a decision later on.
examples.target_text: Ahora estamos muy ocupados, así que tomaremos una decisión más adelante.

examples.en_text: Don't worry, that character appears again later on in the book.
examples.target_text: No te preocupes, ese personaje vuelve a aparecer más adelante en el libro.
